Switching from Profile to Friends (and likely other reads) is slow every time -- there is currently zero caching on backend read endpoints. friends_overview (backend/users/friends.py) runs three uncached DB queries on every call. 215	There is deliberately **no** `DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES`: game-data reads stay unthrottled and only
216	these endpoints pay a cache lookup.
217	
218	**The cache backend is load-bearing, and its failure mode is silent.** DRF stores throttle counters
219	in Django's cache. `LocMemCache` is per-process and every Vercel lambda is its own process, so
220	throttling on it would be near-useless with each cold start resetting the count — and nothing
221	would warn you. `settings.py` therefore tiers the cache: `REDIS_URL` → `RedisCache`; else a real
222	`DATABASE_URL` → `DatabaseCache` (correct, just slower); else `LocMemCache` (local dev only, where
223	single-process makes it accurate). A task must not "simplify" this back to a single LocMemCache.
224	
225	`DatabaseCache` needs its table, created by `manage.py createcachetable` in `backend/vercel.json`'s
226	build command — idempotent, and it must stay there.

1	# Friends & Leaderboard — Caching and Scaling Plan
2	
3	A plan, not a to-do list for right now. Nothing here should be built until a
4	real number (see "When to actually do this") says it's worth it. Written
5	2026-09-19 alongside the friends-search feature, to record the reasoning
6	before it's forgotten.
7	
8	## Where things stand today
9	
10	| Data | Backed by | Cached? |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| Global leaderboard (top 100, rank, total) | `users/leaderboard.py` | **Yes** — Redis ZSET (`leaderboard`, member = public_id, score = points) when `REDIS_URL` is set; falls back to plain Postgres queries otherwise. Already scales to any N via `ZREVRANGE`/`ZREVRANK` (O(log N)). |
13	| Friends leaderboard (`?scope=friends`) | `leaderboard.friends_board()` | No — always Postgres, deliberately (see below). |
14	| Friend list / friend search (`search-friends`) | `users/friends.py` | No — always Postgres. |
15	| Friend requests, blocked list (`friends-overview`) | `users/friends.py` | No — always Postgres. |
16	
17	The global leaderboard cache exists because **N (total players) is
18	unbounded** and a top-100/rank query over the whole table gets slower as the
19	platform grows — a classic case where a sorted-set cache pays for itself.
20	
21	## Why friends data isn't a scaling problem the same way
22	
23	Every friends query is bounded by **your own friend count**, not by the
24	total user base:
25	
26	- `search-friends` resolves "which users are my friends" via two indexed
27	  lookups on `Friendship.user_low`/`user_high` (bounded by your friend
28	  count), *then* filters/paginates that already-small set. It never scans
29	  the whole `CustomUser` table.
30	- `friends_board()` does the same thing before sorting by points.
31	- `friends-overview`'s requests/blocked lists are similarly bounded by
32	  "requests you're personally involved in."
33	
34	No realistic friend count (even a very socially active account) approaches
35	the row counts where an indexed Postgres query over that person's own rows
36	becomes slow. This is different in kind from the global leaderboard, where
37	N is "everyone who has ever signed up." **Caching this today would add
38	invalidation complexity for a problem that doesn't exist yet.**
39	
40	## Where Redis would actually help, if/when it's needed
41	
42	In rough order of when they'd become worth doing, cheapest/highest-value
43	first:
44	
45	1. **Friend-id set per user** — `SADD friends:{public_id} <friend public ids>`.
46	   Turns the "which users are my friends" step from an indexed Postgres
47	   query into an O(1) Redis `SMEMBERS`/`SISMEMBER`. Only worth it if friend
48	   lookups become a measured hot path (e.g. called on every page load
49	   somewhere, not just when the Friends modal is open). Invalidate by
50	   updating both sides' sets on accept/remove/block — mirrors exactly how
51	   `record_score` already updates the leaderboard ZSET on write.
52	
53	2. **`friends_board()` result cache**, short TTL (e.g. 30–60s), keyed by
54	   `friends-board:{public_id}`. Only worth it if the leaderboard modal's
55	   auto-refresh (every 5 min client-side, see `useLeaderboard.ts`) combined
56	   with real traffic produces enough repeated identical queries to matter.
57	   Given the client already caches this for 5 minutes per browser session,
58	   the *server-side* read volume this would save is probably small until
59	   there are many concurrent viewers of the same friend group (unlikely
60	   outside something like a friend-group tournament feature).
61	
62	3. **Friend-request counts** (for a future "N pending requests" badge, if
63	   built) — a natural Redis counter (`INCR`/`DECR` on send/accept/decline),
64	   avoiding a `COUNT(*)` on every page load that shows the badge. This is
65	   the one item here that's "cache because the access pattern demands it,"
66	   not "cache because the query is slow" — worth building alongside
67	   whichever feature first needs a live badge count, not before.

330	## 2026-09-23 — Faster "logged in" on return visits: sonnet vs fable engine
331	Context: card "When I enter the website it takes a long time to see that I am actually logged
332	in" (fullstack, Difficulty override `hard`, title-only spec). Root cause is a post-hydration
333	waterfall in `src/app/providers.tsx` `checkLogin`: Redux starts logged-out, and with a 15-minute
334	access token nearly every return visit does `/me/` (401) → `token/refresh/` (rotation + blacklist
335	write) → `/me/` again, three sequential hops to a cold Vercel serverless Django + Supabase pooler,
336	while `Navigation`/`Landpage` render the guest UI until the last one resolves. Fable was
337	defensible: the fix touches token/session code on the AUTH-9 `risk: high` list, and there are real
338	subtleties — a localStorage read during render is a Next hydration mismatch (must be an effect or
339	a pre-hydration inline script), an optimistic cached user must reconcile without a logout flash,
340	and skipping the dead `/me/` hop means decoding `exp` client-side.
341	Decision: `engineModel: sonnet`, `planModel: fable` (thin spec). The design round can name every
342	mechanism up front — cache the last `/me/` payload under a fixed localStorage key, hydrate the
343	slice optimistically in the mount effect when a refresh token exists, proactively refresh when the
344	access token is expired instead of eating a 401, reconcile with `/me/` in the background, and
345	optionally have `SessionRefreshView` return `user` so it is one hop — each with a done-check.
346	That is long-and-explicit, which is the sonnet row; the AUTH-9 surface is handled by `risk: high`
347	review, not by an engine upgrade.
348	Consequences: auth-bootstrap/perf work stays on sonnet when the design round can pin the
349	hydration-safe read point and the reconcile rules; fable is reserved for cases where the
350	session-state mechanism itself cannot be decided before coding.
351	Design round, same day (`docs/team/designs/2026-09-23-faster-logged-in-state.md`): fourth cloud
352	round with no `Agent` tool and no engine teammates in `ListAgents`, seats filled by the planner
353	from source again. Settled: display-only `nba3via-session-user` cache hydrated via a new
354	`hydrateSession` reducer in the mount effect (never sets `authChecked`); bootstrap decodes `exp`
355	and calls the exported single-flight `refreshSession` directly when expired; `token/refresh/`
356	returns `user`; a 5xx from `/me/` now keeps the session instead of deleting the tokens; a
357	pre-hydration inline script was rejected because `Navigation`'s guest button and user chip are
358	different DOM (the remaining flash is the JS-load window, a follow-up card). Engine stays sonnet.

## 2026-09-29 — Redis-backed read caching (friends_overview first): risk low/sonnet vs risk high/opus
Context: backend card, no override. Spec asks for (1) a researched managed-Redis pick for Vercel
serverless + Supabase transaction pooler, documented in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` with no account or
spend; (2) caching `friends_overview` plus an audit of other hot reads in `users/` and `trivia/`
through Django `CACHES`, with immediate invalidation on friend/request/block actions; (3) correct
behaviour with no Redis (DatabaseCache fallback). Difficulty was never in doubt: multi-endpoint,
a new cached-read + invalidation pattern the app does not have, and it reverses
`docs/CACHING_SCALING_PLAN.md` on two points (that doc says friends data does not need caching yet
and that any cache should follow the raw-client `leaderboard.py` pattern; the owner now wants
`CACHES`). Close call was risk/engine. risk low + sonnet was defensible — it is one app's reads and
the 2026-09-23 entry kept an AUTH-9 task on sonnet. risk high + opus won because `CACHES` in
`settings.py` also stores DRF throttle counters (AUTH_CONSTRAINTS: "the cache backend is
load-bearing, and its failure mode is silent", tiering must not be simplified). A provider that
needs an HTTP client would also change `backend/requirements.txt`, a protected path. And a stale
friends/blocked cache after a block action is a privacy defect, not just a slow read. Since the
2026-09-29 Opus unban, the rubric's "risk: high → opus" override applies, which the 2026-09-23
precedent predates.
Decision: `hard`, `risk: high`, areas backend+auth, `needsDesignRound: true`, `planModel: fable`,
`engineModel: opus` provisional.
Consequences: the design round must (a) pick the provider and say whether it runs over the
`django-redis`/`RedisCache` TCP path or needs a REST client, and name the requirements change if

## 2026-09-29 — Redis-backed read caching (friends_overview first): risk low/sonnet vs risk high/opus
Context: backend card, no override. Spec asks for (1) a researched managed-Redis pick for Vercel
serverless + Supabase transaction pooler, documented in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` with no account or
spend; (2) caching `friends_overview` plus an audit of other hot reads in `users/` and `trivia/`
through Django `CACHES`, with immediate invalidation on friend/request/block actions; (3) correct
behaviour with no Redis (DatabaseCache fallback). Difficulty was never in doubt: multi-endpoint,
a new cached-read + invalidation pattern the app does not have, and it reverses
`docs/CACHING_SCALING_PLAN.md` on two points (that doc says friends data does not need caching yet
and that any cache should follow the raw-client `leaderboard.py` pattern; the owner now wants
`CACHES`). Close call was risk/engine. risk low + sonnet was defensible — it is one app's reads and
the 2026-09-23 entry kept an AUTH-9 task on sonnet. risk high + opus won because `CACHES` in
`settings.py` also stores DRF throttle counters (AUTH_CONSTRAINTS: "the cache backend is
load-bearing, and its failure mode is silent", tiering must not be simplified). A provider that
needs an HTTP client would also change `backend/requirements.txt`, a protected path. And a stale
friends/blocked cache after a block action is a privacy defect, not just a slow read. Since the
2026-09-29 Opus unban, the rubric's "risk: high → opus" override applies, which the 2026-09-23
precedent predates.
Decision: `hard`, `risk: high`, areas backend+auth, `needsDesignRound: true`, `planModel: fable`,
`engineModel: opus` provisional.

`django-redis`/`RedisCache` TCP path or needs a REST client, and name the requirements change if
any; (b) keep the three-tier `CACHES` fallback and throttle behaviour intact; (c) enumerate every
write site that must invalidate each cached key, for both affected users; (d) scope the
`trivia/`/`users/` audit to measured or clearly repeated reads rather than a generic cache layer;
